analyst.summary: Muthoot Finance reported blockbuster FY26 profit and loan-book growth, but a large share of that growth came from gold prices hitting record highs rather than from more customers or more gold being financed - the actual physical gold held as collateral barely grew and even shrank in the most recent quarter. Management's own long-standing growth guidance (15% a year) is far below the headline numbers, and margins are being defended with rate hikes rather than expanding on their own. The core gold-lending business remains healthy and well-capitalized, but the microfinance subsidiary (Belstar) is still working through a loss-making stretch, write-offs have risen sharply, and the stock has already given back roughly a quarter of its value from its 2026 high as the market recognizes the growth is partly a gold-price effect. We rate this a Hold: a sound, well-capitalized franchise, but not one where the recent growth rate should be extrapolated.
